limitations: No claim of zero additional milliseconds or measured speed parity. A success-path observer verifies no response receipt pass and retained inline hashing.
A redirected response without an inline hash may require a full local read when creating its failure-path receipt.
Cancellation, interrupted responses and receipt storage failures do not gain a guaranteed reusable receipt. Existing explicit Restart behavior remains when no valid receipt exists.
Pending publication journals retain ownership; the injected catalog-failure test exercises recovery without creating a competing response receipt. Broader crash/disk-fault qualification remains open.

ASCII PDF notice recognition is a bounded header heuristic, not full PDF validation. It requires a completed HTML/body notice, a standalone numeric version header, whitespace after the closing notice and the existing 2000-byte prefix limit.
The successful paired IDM POST response comparison remains historical 7.45 evidence, not a new 7.47 timing or arbitrary-form equivalence claim.
Native UI and personal-browser acceptance of the new retained plain-form path remain separate from these backend checks.
cleanup: Small fixture outputs retained; old versioned artifacts preserved. Current test executables reuse the shared cache. No previously rejected cleanup was retried.
